memory_lessons.applicability: Compare new rollback arithmetic against both the selected hoisted-weight parent and the shared-denominator sibling; their small timing difference is not evidence for this FMA variant.
memory_lessons.claim: The selected hoisted-weight variant measured 0.29647 s mean and passed all 8 varied cases with maximum absolute error 0.0003281; the shared-denominator variant measured 0.29428 s and passed with maximum absolute error 0.0006638. Both beat the 0.39098 s baseline mean, but neither result predicts this candidate's behavior.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this explicit fused multiply-add candidate for correctness and maximum absolute error on all controller cases, then compare repeated whole-call timings.

proposal.hypothesis: Explicitly fusing the down-weight product with the weighted-sum addition may reduce rollback arithmetic latency and intermediate rounding while preserving the precomputed coefficients and traversal. The prior hoisted-weight parent was correct on all 8 varied cases (maximum absolute error 0.0003281) at 0.29647 s mean; the separate shared-denominator variant was also correct at 0.29428 s. This FMA candidate still requires controller accuracy and whole-call timing measurements.

retained: Use `fmaf(downWeight, V[k], upWeight * V[k + 1])` for the rollback weighted sum, fusing one multiplication and the addition.
Retain the existing precomputed transition weights, descending j traversal, ascending k traversal, and endpoint convention.
